notes: The board and Claude can no longer wipe each other's work. Two things can change your backlog - you, in the board, and Claude - and until now there was only one way to save it, which wrote the WHOLE file. Whoever saved last won everything, and the other side's work vanished with no warning at all. It bit both ways: a board left open for an hour would quietly write its old copy over a card Claude had just added, and Claude could just as easily wipe a card you had typed a minute earlier. This release closes both halves of that. First, there is now a narrow way to save a single card - "change this one card" - merged into whatever is on disk at that moment, so two writers touching different cards cannot collide at all. It works whether or not Stasys is running, which was the long-standing "my edits vanish when the app is closed" complaint. Second, Stasys now stamps each backlog with a revision, and the board quotes it every time it saves: a save built on an out-of-date copy is turned down rather than applied. When that happens the board does not just give up - it takes the newer file, folds your edits into it and saves again, usually within the same second, and you will see a brief "Updated - backlog" note. A card you never touched takes the newer version, a card you did edit keeps yours, and an edit always wins over a delete, so the worst that can happen is a card you deleted coming back, which you can see and simply delete again. Nothing you type is ever silently thrown away, whether the other writer is Claude, a second Stasys window, or someone else on a shared board. The board also no longer forgets: if something changes on disk while you are mid-edit it waits, but it now remembers and picks the change up the moment you are done, instead of never looking again. Nothing about how you use the board changes and your existing cards are untouched.
